current_state.root_cause: Template rotation pipeline produced items overwhelmingly at Understand/Apply levels (97%). Only 10 Analyze items exist (0.39%), and 0 Evaluate items. Very Difficult items require Analyze/Evaluate cognitive design that the pipeline never produced. The existing 85 'Difficult' items earn their label through calculation complexity, not cognitive complexity — 81/85 (95.3%) are at Apply level.

phase_1_emergency_bridge.target: 15-20 recalibrated items to reach ~0.6-0.8% Very Difficult (not the optimistic 2% previously estimated)
phase_1_emergency_bridge.feasibility: LOW — only 4 of 85 Difficult items are at Analyze cognitive level. Recalibrating Apply-level calculation items to Very Difficult would be a psychometric fraud — they lack multi-concept integration, professional judgment, and ambiguous fact patterns required for score 5.
phase_1_emergency_bridge.feasibility_rationale: CAQS v1.0 §1.6 Dimension 3 (Difficulty Calibration) requires that 'the cognitive demand implied by the LOS is consistent with the question's stated difficulty and Bloom's level.' An Apply-level item with a single calculation path cannot be cognitively consistent with Very Difficult, regardless of calculation length.

A__External_Financial_Reporting.rationale: 15% of 254 items. Financial reporting has the richest multi-standard integration opportunities.
best_topics: Comprehensive EPS calculation (basic + diluted + treasury stock + contingently issuable shares)
Multi-standard revenue recognition scenario (ASC 606 5-step with multiple performance obligations, variable consideration, significant financing component)
Statement of cash flows: indirect method with 8+ reconciling items + non-cash disclosure judgment
Comprehensive financial ratio analysis: calculate 5+ ratios from a full set of financial statements, identify which ratios signal which problems, recommend action
Inventory + LCM + purchase commitments: combined scenario requiring multiple GAAP applications
Long-lived assets: impairment testing (ASC 360) + depreciation change in estimate + asset retirement obligation in one scenario
Equity method + OCI + fair value option: scenario where candidate identifies correct classification for multiple investments
Income tax: deferred tax asset valuation allowance + uncertain tax position + rate change in one scenario

B__Planning_Budgeting_Forecasting.rationale: 20% of 254 items. Budgeting is inherently multi-step and integrative — ideal for Very Difficult.
best_topics: Comprehensive master budget cascade: sales → production → DM → DL → OH → COGS → S&A → cash budget → pro forma statements (multi-item set)
Cash budget with: collections pattern + disbursements timing + minimum balance + line of credit + interest calculation + sensitivity to 20% sales drop
Flexible budget performance report: parse 3 columns (static, flexible, actual), identify all variances, isolate volume vs. price vs. efficiency
Zero-based budgeting implementation scenario: evaluate 4 decision packages with cost-benefit, rank by strategic priority
Probabilistic budgeting: expected value with 3 scenarios, sensitivity to probability changes, identify key assumption risk
Rolling forecast vs. traditional annual budget: evaluate scenario where candidate identifies which approach fits the business context
Learning curve + production budget + staffing: combined scenario where learning curve affects labor hours which affects production budget which affects hiring
Kaizen budgeting + variance analysis: continuous improvement targets with variance investigation thresholds

C__Performance_Management.rationale: 20% of 254 items. Performance management has the richest existing Difficult cluster (37 items in Section C at DS=4).
best_topics: Comprehensive 4-variance analysis: spending + efficiency + budget + volume for both variable and fixed OH on one scenario
Mix + yield variance: 3-product sales mix variance with market size + market share decomposition
Transfer pricing with capacity constraint: 3 divisions, one at capacity, negotiate transfer price considering opportunity cost + market price + variable cost + dual rate
ROI vs. Residual Income conflict: division manager rejects project that's good for company but hurts division ROI — candidate evaluates decision
Balanced scorecard: given 4 perspectives with 12 metrics, identify which 2 metrics show performance gap, recommend strategic initiative
Customer profitability analysis (multi-dimensional): cost-to-serve + product mix + pricing strategy
Segment reporting: contribution margin format with traceable vs. common fixed costs, make-or-drop decision with segment margin analysis
Productivity + efficiency + effectiveness: integrated scenario with OEE, labor productivity, material yield

D__Cost_Management.rationale: 15% of 254 items. Cost management has natural multi-concept integration opportunities.
best_topics: Comprehensive CVP: 3 products with different CM ratios + tax rate + target after-tax income + sensitivity to 10% price change + operating leverage calculation
Relevant costing decision matrix: make-or-buy + special order + drop-segment + product-mix-constraint (4 decisions, one scenario)
Joint product: 3 products, allocate via NRV + physical measures + constant GM%, then sell-or-process-further decision for each
ABC vs. traditional costing: same company, compare product costs under both methods, identify which products are over/under-costed, recommend pricing change
Service department cost allocation: 3 service departments, 2 production departments, use direct + step + reciprocal methods, compare results
Process costing with spoilage: weighted average + FIFO, normal vs. abnormal spoilage, transferred-in costs
Theory of Constraints: identify bottleneck, calculate throughput per constraint unit, determine optimal product mix, evaluate capacity expansion

E__Internal_Controls.rationale: 15% of 254 items. Internal controls currently has 0 Difficult items and 0 Analyze items — the most severe gap. Rich opportunity for scenario-based evaluation items.
best_topics: COSO ERM scenario evaluation: 5-component analysis of a company's risk management, identify missing components, recommend improvements
Fraud triangle analysis: scenario with pressure, opportunity, rationalization indicators — candidate identifies which element is most acute and recommends control
Segregation of duties in ERP: 4 roles, 8 transactions, candidate identifies SoD conflicts and proposes role reconfiguration
Control deficiency classification: 3 deficiencies in one scenario — classify each as deficiency/significant deficiency/material weakness, explain threshold
COSO Internal Control evaluation: assess control environment + risk assessment + control activities + information/communication + monitoring from a narrative scenario
IT general controls vs. application controls: 6 controls in a scenario, classify each, identify control gaps
Foreign Corrupt Practices Act compliance: scenario with international operations, identify FCPA risks, recommend compliance controls
Whistleblower + ethics + governance: scenario where candidate evaluates whether the control environment supports ethical reporting

F__Technology_and_Analytics.rationale: 13% of 254 items. Technology items tend to be definitional — need scenario-based evaluation to reach Very Difficult.
best_topics: Data analytics interpretation: given regression output + correlation matrix + trend data, candidate diagnoses business problem and recommends action
ERP implementation risk assessment: 4 modules, 3 business units, identify implementation risks, recommend phased rollout
Cybersecurity control evaluation: incident scenario, candidate classifies attack type, identifies control failure, recommends remediation
Business intelligence dashboard design: 6 candidate KPIs, only 4 slots — candidate selects the 4 most decision-relevant metrics and justifies exclusion
AI/automation governance: scenario where candidate evaluates whether an automated decision system has appropriate human oversight
Data governance maturity assessment: evaluate a company's data management practices against a maturity model, identify gaps
Blockchain/smart contract: scenario evaluating whether blockchain adds value for a specific supply chain use case

multi_select_with_subtle_distinctions.description: Items where 3 of 5-6 choices are correct. Distractors are not 'obviously wrong' — they represent plausible but incorrect applications. Tests ability to distinguish between similar but distinct concepts.
multi_select_with_subtle_distinctions.example: A company shows declining gross margin but rising net income. Which 3 of the following 5 explanations are plausible? (A) Increased volume offset margin decline (B) SG&A as % of revenue decreased (C) COGS increased in absolute dollars (D) Other income increased significantly (E) Tax rate decreased from 25% to 21%. Answer: B, D, E.

numeric_with_multi_exhibit_dependency.description: Items requiring data from 2-3 exhibits (e.g., P&L + balance sheet + footnote) to compute a result. Candidate must identify which data is relevant and discard which is not. Ambiguous fact pattern.
numeric_with_multi_exhibit_dependency.example: Given (Exhibit 1) Income Statement, (Exhibit 2) Balance Sheet, and (Exhibit 3) Footnote on operating leases: Calculate the company's adjusted debt-to-equity ratio after capitalizing operating leases. Include only leases with terms > 12 months.

scenario_based_evaluation.description: Items presenting a business scenario where the candidate must evaluate competing recommendations. All options are defensible — only one is optimal given the specific constraints.
scenario_based_evaluation.example: Division A is at capacity. Division B wants to buy internally at variable cost. Division A can sell externally at market price. Which transfer pricing approach maximizes company-wide profit while maintaining divisional autonomy?

select_with_judgment_component.description: Single-best-answer items where all distractors represent legitimate approaches, and the candidate must apply professional judgment to select the best one given nuanced criteria.
select_with_judgment_component.example: A company has 3 capital projects with NPV of $500K, $450K, and $400K respectively, but only $800K in available capital. The $400K project has strategic importance for entering a new market. What is the BEST recommendation?

fill_in_blank_with_judgment.description: Open-response items requiring numeric answer derived from multi-step calculation with judgment about which inputs to use.
fill_in_blank_with_judgment.example: Given a scenario with both absorption and variable costing income statements, a special order, and a capacity constraint: What is the minimum acceptable price for the special order? [no answer choices provided — candidate computes independently]

criteria: Integrates 3+ distinct CMA Part 1 concepts (not just multi-step of same concept)
Requires professional judgment — not just mechanical calculation
Has ambiguous fact pattern where candidate must identify what is relevant and discard distractors
Takes 3-4 minutes to solve (time pressure component)
Distractors are highly plausible — each represents a documented misconception or plausible alternative approach
At least one distractor is the result of a common but incorrect calculation path
Explanation must be a mini-lesson: concept, solution, distractor analysis, exam trap, business application

must_not: Single-step calculation with large numbers (does not make it Very Difficult)
Generic scenario with no business context
Explanation that only states the formula
must: Named company with realistic business scenario
At least 2 exhibits providing data the candidate must interpret
At least 1 piece of data in exhibits that is NOT needed (tests relevance filtering)
At least 2 distractors that are the result of genuine calculation paths a candidate might follow

r_series_opportunity.description: Pack E's 40 R-series items (P1-E-R01 through P1-E-R40) were authored independently of the template rotation pipeline. They have exceptionally long ExplanationCorrect fields (900-1450 chars vs. pool average ~150) suggesting rich educational content. However, they are all currently labeled Moderate or below with no Analyze cognitive level. KEY OPPORTUNITY: These items have deep explanations but were never assigned appropriate difficulty. Upgrading the most complex 8-10 R-series items with additional multi-exhibit scenarios and judgment components could produce high-quality Very Difficult items with less effort than creating new items from scratch.
r_series_opportunity.recommendation: Target 8-10 R-series items for enhancement to Very Difficult level as part of Phase 1 bridge.

section_e_emergency.recommendation: Prioritize Pack E Section E in Phase 2 content creation. The COSO ERM and fraud assessment topics are naturally suited to Evaluate-level items.

pack_a_gap.recommendation: Pack A needs the most Phase 2 creation. The financial reporting domain (Section A) has the richest multi-standard integration opportunities.

cross_reference_analysis.relationship_to_dl031: DL-031 (Definition-Match Difficulty Inflation) found ~500 items systemically over-labeled as Moderate. The same template pipeline that inflated Moderate items also failed to produce any Analyze/Evaluate items. Both defects share the same root cause: template-based labeling without cognitive assessment.
cross_reference_analysis.relationship_to_dl032: DL-032 (Case Bank Uniform Difficulty) found 0/745 case items above Moderate. Case studies are naturally suited to Very Difficult — they inherently have multi-exhibit dependency and scenario-based evaluation. Case study difficulty recalibration should be a parallel workstream.
cross_reference_analysis.relationship_to_dl030: DL-030 (CorrectChoice Answer-Key Errors) found 5 Certified items with wrong answers. Any Phase 1 recalibration must include an independent answer-key verification for each upgraded item — ensuring we don't promote items with unknown correctness defects.
cross_reference_analysis.relationship_to_dl035: DL-035 (Governance Guard DL-026 Coverage Gap) found 39 Certified items with empty distractor EW slots. Very Difficult items require robust distractor explanations — empty slots at this difficulty level would be catastrophic for learner experience.

final_recommendation.summary: The Very Difficult gap (0 of 254 target) is the most severe calibration deficit in the entire inventory. It CANNOT be closed through recalibration alone — there are fewer than 10 items at the Analyze cognitive level that could plausibly support a Very Difficult label. Full remediation requires a dedicated content authoring sprint creating ~250 new items at Analyze/Evaluate cognitive levels with multi-concept integration, multi-exhibit dependency, and professional judgment components.
final_recommendation.phase_1_decision: IMMEDIATELY EXECUTE — recalibrate 4 Analyze-level items, enhance 10 Tier 2 items, upgrade 8 R-series items. These 22 items provide a bridge to ~0.9% while Phase 2 content creation ramps up.
final_recommendation.phase_2_decision: COMMISSION — authorize a dedicated Very Difficult content authoring sprint. The 254-item target requires 6-8 weeks of dedicated authoring. Prioritize Section E (Internal Controls, worst gap) and Section B/C (richest topic foundation).
final_recommendation.minimum_acceptable_bridge: For the CMA exam simulator to have any Very Difficult presence, Phase 1a-b MUST be completed before any learner uses the simulator in a timed full-length exam mode. 0% Very Difficult means the difficulty distribution is completely unrepresentative of the actual CMA exam.
final_recommendation.quality_warning: Under no circumstances should Apply-level calculation items be recalibrated to Very Difficult as a 'numbers game' to hit the 10% target. Psychometric integrity requires that the difficulty label reflects genuine cognitive demand. A pool of 254 'Very Difficult' items that are all just long calculations will not prepare candidates for the judgment-intensive questions on the actual CMA Part 1 exam.
